1.why: 26/28/32 are even and 29 is the lone odd value in the set.

2.why: 8%, 20% and 10% are integers; 4.5% is the only value carrying a decimal.

3.why: 6/12 and 3/12 are unreduced so unlikely to be an authored key, leaving 5/12 and 7/12 indistinguishable.

4.why: two complement pairs (8/25+17/25, 2/5+3/5) cancel out; picked the one value that is neither a fifth nor a complement of a fifth.

5.why: 10, 13, 16 form an arithmetic run of 3 with 6 outside it, and 13 is the median of that run.

6.why: 69.5 is the scale outlier, but nothing separates 29.5, 34.25 and 26.75.

7.why: 2/15 is exactly the product of two other options (2/3 x 1/5), the classic composed value in a four-option set.

8.why: two tight pairs (30/40 and 74/84) with no lone value; nothing structural separates them.

9.why: a fully crossed 2x2 of numerators {3,7} by denominators {10,13} - no option is distinguished.

10.why: 4/16 is unreduced and so an unlikely authored key, but 15/16, 5/16 and 11/16 are otherwise alike.

11.why: all four are binomial coefficients (210, 35, 15, 126) and none stands out.

12.why: the sixteenths pair 43.75/56.25 looks like the computed branch against round 75/25, but the pair itself is a coin flip.

13.why: 71, 74, 77 is an arithmetic run of 3 with 104 far outside; 74 is its median.

14.why: three options are fifteenths (5, 7, 8) and 12/25 is off-denominator, but 7/15 vs 8/15 is undecidable.

15.why: denominators 5, 4, 12, 20 with no lone decimal, square or derived value.

16.why: 12, 20 and 60 are even and share the 60-divisor family; 27 is the lone odd value and a perfect cube.

17.why: the set {6, 9, 11, 14} is symmetric about 10 (6+14 = 9+11 = 20), so no option is singled out.

18.why: eighths with 1/2 the reduced form of 4/8; all four are reduced and equally plausible.

19.why: 27/125 is the only option that is a clean cube, (3/5)^3, over a cube denominator; 50/125 is unreduced.

20.why: 1/2, 2/3, 3/4, 5/6 are four ordinary reduced fractions with no structural outlier.

21.why: 9 is the only perfect square among 3, 24, 9, 11.

22.why: all four are thirty-sixths forming two exact complement pairs (10+26, 15+21), so the set is balanced.

23.why: the four values are the run 7/20, 8/20, 9/20, 10/20; only 2/5 and 1/2 appear reduced and 1/2 reads as the naive trap.

24.why: the set is built from p = 2/5: 3/5 is 1-p, 4/25 is p^2, and 21/25 is the uniquely two-step value 1-p^2.
